skill_entry.name: 14. A behavior change that presents as a refactor, cleanup, one-character edit or debug-value revert
skill_entry.trigger: A hunk in h/ or src/ (never t/) of one of five shapes, with no PR-body sentence or in-hunk comment naming an input on which old and new behave differently: (a) a same-type expression swap on an executable line: an index or lookup (`x.i` to `positions[x]`), a literal used as a comparison, divisor, multiplier, sleep argument or default, a comparison operator, or a negation; (b) a removed `isnan`, `isfinite`, `isinf` or `infinity()` line while the hunk adds a helper call whose result feeds `>` or `<` against a tolerance; (c) a sleep, wait, assert, lock or check turned into a `//` comment; (d) a changed named constant that a reader compares a measured time or count against; (e) a changed comparison that resolves a build or environment default while the comment block above keeps the old meaning.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. Pre-filter, never a finding: per hunk join removed and added lines, tokenize, keep pairs with at most 2 removed and 8 added tokens; drop string-literal edits, argument-list changes, type swaps, `#if`/`#define` lines, names the diff declares, one-member typedef wraps, same-value literal-to-constant swaps, inserted statements. 2. Shape (a): read both definitions at HEAD; write the coincidence condition and one differing input; none means no finding. 3. Shape (b): read the helper's NaN and inf returns; evaluate the consuming comparison (`NaN > tol` is false). 4. Shape (c): confirm no identical call is added elsewhere in the diff. 5. Shape (d): quote every reader that logs, errors or exits on a crossing; class it fatal or log-and-continue. 6. Shape (e): read the comment block, the `#define` default and the cited doc. 7. Grep the PR body, then the commit messages, for the old and new spelling.
skill_entry.question: On which input do the removed line and the added line behave differently, and does the PR body say that difference is intended?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A PR-body sentence or in-hunk comment naming the differing input class and calling the old line wrong (PR 2698 `0` to `no_readback_sentinel`, body line 9); a commit message alone never clears (1fd45e6062 named 'multiple branches' four days before Wade asked). A literal or constant change the title or body states (tron-1739 'Set page size to 128'; PR 2766 'larger max_cmd_fifo_depth'; PR 2698 'Debug-value reverts' for maxpolls, whose reader errors and exits), except a lowered limit whose reader logs and continues. A commented-out call whose identical text is added elsewhere in the diff (tron-2008, wait moved into the callees). A bare literal replacing a named value (magic-literal check, 3307459854). Removed special-value lines found verbatim at HEAD (a move). A `#define` flip (debug-switch check). Any hunk in t/.
skill_entry.finding_shape: `<file>:<line>` changes `<old>` to `<new>`. So on <input class> the code now <new behavior> where it used to <old behavior>; the PR body does not say this is intended<; commit <id> says '<quote>'>. was this intentional? If so, please say under which inputs the old line was wrong. Shape (b): don't we still need to handle NaN / inf for the comparison to be trustworthy? Shape (d): the reader at <file:line> logs on a crossing; which values have we seen on this branch, and in main? Siblings of one swap get one sentence pointing at the first finding. No value, remedy or benchmark is proposed.
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: normal when the swap is in a production path: a plain question ('was this intentional?', 'were we grabbing the (potentially) wrong token-id all this time?', 'don't we still need to consider nan / inf values?'). When a bot already flagged it he writes one line with no severity word, either endorsing ('Cursorbot's observation seems valid', 3307473806) or asking the author directly ('was this intentional?', 3463061252, after a cursor[bot] High Severity). For a threshold he labels his own prediction as speculation and addresses the people who know the runtime ('I'm speculating we'll see a LOT more... not saying that's a reason to keep the larger value', 3236579299). Never blocking: he approved PR 1997 nine minutes after the NaN question (00:43:21Z to 00:52:27Z) and PR 2766 with 'Approved, assuming you'll follow up on the remaining minor comments'.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file (the definitions of both expressions, the comment block and `#define` above a changed comparison); other files (the helper the added line calls, every reader of a changed constant via git grep, the struct behind a typedef wrap); PR body and commit messages (a body sentence clears, a commit sentence is quoted); runtime (a log line already observed on the branch when the user gives logs; otherwise Insufficient data).

## Check 14: a behavior change that presents as a refactor, cleanup, one-character edit or debug-value revert

Setup for this check: BASE is the PR's recorded base, not origin/main.
`BASE=$(gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json baseRefOid -q .baseRefOid)`; for an open PR whose base branch moved, `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/<baseRefName>`. On PR 2176 (base branch hwattention_sync) merge-base against origin/main gives 83 files instead of the PR's 20.
`git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src > c14.diff`

1. Pre-filter (a candidate list, never a finding). Save as step1.py, run `python3 -I step1.py c14.diff`:
```
import sys,re,difflib
TOK=re.compile(r'\w+|\S')
def hunks(p):
    f=h=None; out=[]
    for l in open(p,errors='replace'):
        l=l.rstrip('\n')
        if l.startswith('+++ '): f=l[6:]; continue
        if l.startswith('--- '): continue
        if l.startswith('@@'):
            if h: out.append(h)
            h={'file':f,'line':int(re.search(r'\+(\d+)',l).group(1)),'old':[],'new':[]}; continue
        if h is None: continue
        if l.startswith('-'): h['old'].append(l[1:].strip())
        elif l.startswith('+'): h['new'].append(l[1:].strip())
    if h: out.append(h)
    return out
cmt=lambda s: s.startswith(('//','*','/*'))
tot=kept=0
for h in hunks(sys.argv[1]):
    if not h['old'] or not h['new'] or h['file'].startswith('t/') or not h['file'].endswith(('.hpp','.cpp','.h','.cc')): continue
    if all(cmt(l) for l in h['old']+h['new']): continue
    tot+=1
    o=TOK.findall(' '.join(h['old'])); n=TOK.findall(' '.join(h['new']))
    rem=add=0
    for t,i1,i2,j1,j2 in difflib.SequenceMatcher(a=o,b=n,autojunk=False).get_opcodes():
        if t!='equal': rem+=i2-i1; add+=j2-j1
    if 0<rem+add and rem<=2 and add<=8:
        kept+=1; print(f"{h['file']}:{h['line']} rem={rem} add={add} | {' '.join(h['old'])[:100]} -> {' '.join(h['new'])[:100]}")
print(f"pairs={tot} kept={kept}")
```
   Joining the lines of one hunk matters: PR 2176's `size_t tok_ix = enclosing_state.token_positions[...]` is wrapped over two `+` lines, and a line-by-line pairing never sees one expression. Then drop, by reading each kept line once: (i) the change is inside a string literal; (ii) tokens only added to or removed from an argument, parameter or capture list; (iii) a type name swapped in a declaration (`float` to `double`, `uint32_t` to `process_device_id`); (iv) `#if`, `#ifdef`, `#define` lines (debug-switch check); (v) the new name is declared in the diff (rename map, a new accessor `used` to `used()`, a new setter `set_node(...)`); (vi) a strong typedef wrapped or unwrapped (`x` to `x.i`, `T{x}`) whose struct holds one data member: `git -C WT grep -n 'struct <T>' HEAD -- h`, once per type; (vii) a literal replaced by a named constant with the same value at HEAD (magic-literal check); (viii) an inserted statement (added tokens contain `;` or `{`). Name the pair, kept and surviving counts in the report.
2. Shape (b): `grep -n -E '^-.*(isnan|isfinite|isinf|infinity\(\))' c14.diff`; for each hit `git -C WT grep -n -F -- '<removed line>' HEAD -- h src` (a verbatim hit at HEAD is a move; drop). Otherwise list the `+` lines of the same hunk matching `\b(comberr|abserr|relerr|approx_equal|is_close)\s*\(` and the `>` or `<` comparison that consumes the result; read the helper at HEAD and write its return for a NaN on either side and for an inf on one side; evaluate the comparison with that value.
3. Shape (c): `grep -n -E '^\+\s*//\s*(usleep|sleep|nanosleep|wait\w*|mwaitx|TRON_ASSERT|assert|lock|unlock|check\w*)\s*\(' c14.diff` (the `\(` keeps prose comments such as `// mwaitx-waitable views` out); confirm the same text is a `-` line of the hunk; then `grep -c -F '+  <call text>' c14.diff`: a replacement call added elsewhere means the statement moved (do not fire).
4. Shape (d): `grep -E '^[-+]\s*(inline )?(static )?constexpr' c14.diff | sed -E 's/^([-+]).*\b(\w+)\s*=\s*([0-9]+).*/\1 \2 \3/' | awk '{k=$2; if($1=="-") o[k]=$3; else n[k]=$3} END{for(k in o) if(k in n && o[k]!=n[k]) print k, o[k], "->", n[k]}'` (a name with the same value on both sides is a moved constant, not a change). For each name `git -C WT grep -n '<constant>' HEAD -- h src`; quote every reader with `spdlog::|debug_exit|TRON_ASSERT` within 5 lines of the comparison and class it fatal (error then exit) or log-and-continue. A constant no reader compares a measured value against (a ring size, a page size, a max layer count) is not a candidate.
5. Shape (e): `grep -n -E '^[-+].*(DEFAULT_ON|_DEFAULT|_ENABLED|DEFAULT).*(!=|==) *[01]\b' c14.diff`; keep only a `-`/`+` pair of the same line (the draft's `return (true|false);` alternative matched 7 added lines on PR 3016 and 2 on tron-2875 that resolve no default). `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<line-15>,<line>p'` for the comment block and the `#define`; `grep -n '<MACRO>' doc/*.md`.
6. Shape (a) definitions: `git -C WT grep -n -E '<old container>;|<new container>;' HEAD -- h`, `git -C WT grep -n 'struct <type>' HEAD -- h` (read the comment on validity), `git -C WT grep -n '<new container>.push_back' HEAD -- h src` (the fill site); write the coincidence condition and one differing input. No differing input, no finding.
7. Intent: `grep -n -i -E '<old token>|<new token>|intention|deliberate|debug-only|revert' body.md`: a body sentence that names the input class, or lists the value change, clears. `git -C WT log --format='%h %s%n%b' BASE..HEAD | grep -n -i -E '<old token>|<new token>'`: a commit sentence does not clear; quote it in the finding and ask for it in the body or at the line.
8. Observed values (shape d): `grep -rn '<log string>' <run logs>` only when the user gives logs; otherwise write `Insufficient data: no run log` and quote the reader line.
9. One finding per hunk, phrased as a question with both behaviors on the named input; siblings with the same removed and added tokens get one pointer sentence.

final.widen_delta: None of the thirteen existing checks compares the old and new behavior of a same-type expression swap; check 10 asks whether a hunk belongs to the PR, check 1 cites the NaN rule for test rows only. This is a new check 14. Boundaries with neighbours: (1) disabled-code-left-in keeps a commented-out call that has a live replacement in the same diff (tron-2008 pattern, and 2737935271's reference copy next to a live call); shape (c) takes a commented-out sleep, wait, assert, lock or check only when no replacement call exists in the diff. (2) magic-literal keeps a named value replaced by a bare literal (3307459854, `timeout_ns` -> `1000`) and a literal replaced by a same-value named constant (PR 2176 hwattention.hpp:848 `128` -> `hwkv_tok_per_page`); check 14 keeps a literal replaced by another literal of the same constant (`usleep(10)` -> `usleep(1)`, `10000000000` -> `100000000`). (3) claim-wider-than-code (3501641254) owns an unchanged fallback literal that contradicts a stated default; shape (e) owns the changed comparison line (memory.cpp:80); when both fire on one PR, report once under check 14 and cite the doc line from claim-wider. (4) debug-switch keeps `#if`, `#ifdef` and `#define` flips. (5) verify-automated-findings lists 3463061252 and 3307473806 as endorsements, not members; no conflict. Setup changes: the common setup's `BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base $HEAD origin/main)` is wrong for a PR whose base is another branch (PR 2176 on hwattention_sync: 83 files instead of 20); use `gh pr view N --json baseRefOid` first. Setup step 2 should say the NaN rule applies to production comparison helpers as well as to test rows (codex C11), and date it: CLAUDE.md 0b094959a7 (2026-04-16, 'NaN always indicates corruption'), moved to AGENTS.md on 2026-08-07 (942d4e3f5a, b55feb29a5 'Treat NaN as corruption'); cite it only for a PR after those dates. Check 10's do-not-fire 'differs only by the rename map' is reused verbatim as drop rule (v).

changes_made: Step 1 rewritten (FACTS P1/P2, EXEC problems 2-3, PRECISION problem 4): the awk+python pipeline that kept 0 pairs is replaced by a per-hunk script that joins the removed lines and the added lines, tokenizes, and keeps pairs with at most 2 removed and 8 added tokens. Decided among three proposals by measurement: EXEC's '<=10 total tokens' keeps more non-swaps (24/39 on PR 2176, 29/101 on PR 3016); FACTS's step 1b (same prefix up to `=` or `(`) is a special case of the joined rule; PRECISION's 'added tokens form one bracketed lookup' is covered by the drop rules. The adopted rule reaches all five PR 2176 swaps (self_attention.hpp:859-860, model.hpp:1446, :1493, llama.hpp:988, :1042), memory.cpp:80, maxpolls and usleep 10->1.

Step 1 gained eight mechanical drop rules (PRECISION problems 5-6, 10; EXEC fix 3): string-literal edits, argument/parameter/capture-list changes, type swaps in declarations, #if/#define lines, diff-declared names (check 10's rename-map wording), one-member typedef wraps (tron-3756, 55 pairs, struct process_device_id { size_t i; }), same-value literal-to-constant swaps (PR 2176 hwattention.hpp:848), inserted statements; plus the C++-extension file filter (tron-1707 CMakeLists, tron-1727 shell hits). Explicit exit added: no differing input, no finding.

Open question 1 answered with measurements at the correct bases (FACTS F4, with FACTS P3's PR 2176 numbers replaced: its 207 pairs came from a merge-base against origin/main; the PR's base 363edb2910 gives 39 pairs): PR 3016 101 pairs / 19 kept / 2 survive (1 Wade's), PR 2176 39 / 22 / 5 (one family), PR 2698 6 / 3 / 1, PR 2766 25 / 4 / 1, 15 silent diffs 0 survivors.

Trigger shape (a) narrowed to an executable line (comparison, divisor, multiplier, sleep argument, default) and shape (d) to a constant a reader compares a measured time or count against (PRECISION fixes 1 and 5); tron-1739 page_size and tron-1707 kv_xfer_ring_size no longer fire.

do_not_fire split into two intent outcomes (EXEC fix 8, decided against the draft after reading 1fd45e6062's body: 'diverges from the absolute tree position when multiple branches are visited', 2026-03-13, before Wade's first review commit 9553cd0a11): a PR-body sentence or in-hunk comment clears; a commit message alone is quoted in the finding and does not clear. Finding shape changed to 'the PR body does not say this is intended<; commit <id> says ...>' so it is true in both outcomes (EXEC fix 9).

do_not_fire gained: a commented-out call whose identical text is added elsewhere in the diff (PRECISION fix 3, tron-2008 hwattention.hpp:816 and :847 with the call added at :683 and :765; line numbers recomputed from the hunk headers, PRECISION's :848/:767 were off by one or two); a literal or constant change the title or body states (PRECISION fix 4, verified new case PR 2766 body line 19 'larger max_cmd_fifo_depth' with a measured-count reader at worker.cpp:988, Wade silent); the lowered-limit exception kept for a log-and-continue reader.

Debug-value revert sentence corrected (FACTS P7/F8): the maxpolls reader at 159e09a940 src/pos/worker.cpp:413-422 logs spdlog::error then debug_exit (fatal); the distinction is fatal versus log-and-continue (driver.cpp:1056-1058), not 'no log fires'.

3307459854 sentence corrected (FACTS P6/F7, PRECISION overlap): a bare literal replacing a named value, or in a new call whose siblings pass a named value, goes to the magic-literal check; check 14 keeps literal-to-literal changes of the same constant.

Step 2 narrowed (EXEC fix 5): a verbatim `git grep -F` of the removed line at HEAD detects a move (PR 2176: 5 lines, all in hwattention_dump.hpp); the helper regex now requires `\s*\(` and drops `close|within` (which matched `out.close()` and prose).
Step 3 regex now requires `\s*\(` after the keyword (the head diff of PR 2766 matched the prose comment `// mwaitx-waitable views`) and adds the replacement-call grep.
